reasoning:
The U.S. economy as of August 28, 2026 firmly occupies the Recovery phase, confirmed by a Composite Growth Z-score of +0.257 (expansionary) paired with a Composite Inflation Z-score of -0.340 (disinflationary). All major growth indicators are strongly positive: Atlanta Fed GDPNow projects Q3 2026 real GDP at +4.6% annualized, ISM Manufacturing reached 55.6 in July (its highest reading since May 2022), initial jobless claims sit at 203,000 per week (near historic lows), and the S&P 500 is up 12.8% YTD. The non-inverted yield curve (10Y-2Y spread: +47bps) and robust ISM Services (54.1, 25th consecutive month of expansion) reinforce the above-trend growth narrative without recessionary signals. Confidence is calibrated at 68 rather than higher because meaningful tensions persist: Core PCE at 3.3% YoY and PPI Final Demand at 4.99% remain materially above target, and Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech (August 28) has driven market-implied September rate-hike probability to ~60%, creating a policy misalignment unusual for Recovery-phase conditions.

The 6-month trajectory shows a clear clockwise rotation: from Recovery (Feb 2026) through Overheat peak (Apr-May 2026, inflation Z at +0.763) and back into Recovery (Jul-Aug 2026, inflation Z at -0.604 then -0.340). The inflation Z-score is now rising from its trough, narrowing from -0.604 in July to -0.340 in August — a clockwise signal suggesting gradual movement toward the Overheat boundary. Growth simultaneously re-accelerated from +0.131 (June) to +0.257 (August), confirming the expansion is intact and the clock hand is advancing clockwise from 305° (last week) to 307° (current). The trajectory points toward a potential Overheat transition within 1-3 months if PPI pipeline pressures begin transmitting into consumer prices and GDPNow remains elevated.
outlook: Over the next 3-6 months (October 2026 through February 2027), the balance of evidence favors a clockwise continuation of the Investment Clock cycle. The base case (~45% probability) is a transition into the Overheat phase by Q4 2026 as GDPNow's 4.6% Q3 strength sustains above-trend output and PPI pipeline inflation (4.7-5% YoY) begins passing through to consumer prices, pushing the inflation Z-score back above zero. A secondary scenario (~35% probability) anticipates continued Recovery as the September FOMC hike is absorbed without major disruption and inflation remains just below zero Z-score for another quarter. The critical risk scenario (~20%) involves a Fed policy error — aggressive tightening via a September and November hike sequence — that suppresses investment and triggers a growth deceleration, potentially stalling or reversing the clockwise trajectory toward Reflation. Key catalysts to monitor in order of importance: (1) August CPI/PCE releases (September 11 and 26) for evidence of PPI pass-through; (2) September FOMC decision (September 15-16) and dot plot for rate path clarity; (3) August Nonfarm Payrolls (September 4) following July's concerning -23,000 print; (4) ISM Manufacturing/Services for August (September 1 and 3). A sustained S&P 500 above its current levels and 5-year breakeven inflation below 2.5% would validate the Recovery-to-Overheat transition thesis.

gemini_research_summary: The U.S. economy is firmly in the Recovery phase as of August 28, 2026, with above-trend growth (GDPNow Q3: +4.6%, ISM Mfg: 55.6 — highest since May 2022) and below-trend inflation (Core CPI: 2.15% YoY) confirming the quantitative signals. However, Core PCE remains sticky at 3.3% YoY and PPI at ~5% creates pipeline inflation risk, while Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech has driven September rate-hike probability to ~60%, creating an atypical policy tightening environment within a Recovery phase. Historical analogs to 1995-96 and 2016-17 support continued equity outperformance, but the restrictive starting rate environment and PPI pressures increase the probability of either a premature Overheat transition or a policy-induced mid-cycle slowdown within the next 1-3 months.
